newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-OLAJUWON HOSPITALIZED AGAIN FOR IRREGULAR HEARTBEAT.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-OLAJUWON HOSPITALIZED AGAIN FOR IRREGULAR HEARTBEAT.

text.p: Houston Rockets superstar centre Hakeem Olajuwon has been hospitalized for the second time in less than two weeks with an irregular heartbeat.
Olajuwon flew to Houston from Washington Sunday to be admitted to Methodist Hospital, where spokeswoman Angela McPike said Olajuwon was in "very good condition."
The Nigerian-born U.S. citizen had 34 points and 17 rebounds in Houston's 103-99 win at Washington Saturday night.
Olajuwon was also admitted to Methodist Hospital after a November 19 game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.
An exercise stress test and an echocardiogram were both normal and Olajuwon was released from the hospital two days later.
Olajuwon rested for a week and missed three games. Houston went 3-0 in Olajuwon's absence, defeating Phoenix and winning at Golden State and Los Angeles against the Lakers.
Olajuwon returned last Tuesday and scored 21 points in Houston's 102-101 overtime victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.
Olajuwon had 17 points and 13 rebounds in a 120-94 win at Boston Friday night and followed with a 34-point, 17-rebound performance against the Bullets Saturday.
Olajuwon missed seven games early in the 1991-92 season due to similar heartrate problems.
He has had clotting problems and was treated with blood thinners and has worn an elastic sleeve on his leg to improve circulation. Olajuwon suffered from anaemia late in the 1994-95 season.

The 33-year-old Olajuwon is an 11-time All-Star who won the Most Valuable Player Award in 1994 and led the Rockets to consecutive NBA championships in 1994 and 1995. He was a member of the U.S. Olympic gold-medal Dream Team in Atlanta this summer.
Olajuwon is not the only player with heart problems.
The San Antonio Spurs keep a defibrillator machine at courtside for forward Monty Williams, who has an irregular heartbeat.
Philadelphia 76ers forward Derrick Coleman missed the first month of the 1995-96 season with an irregular heartbeat but has been unaffected since.

Boston Celtics guard Reggie Lewis collapsed during a playoff game and was advised to retire by a team of doctors. He sought a second opinion from a doctor who cleared him to play, and died while shooting baskets three months later.
Hank Gathers, a college star for Loyola Marymount, collapsed and died on the court in 1990.
